validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE = confirmed by two independent sources. (1) The sheet's own primary citation, Al-Jibawi 'Shedding Light on Recent Oil & Gas Pipeline Projects in Iraq' (iraqieconomists.net, dated June 2025 in the URL path, compiled from OPC/SCOP declarations): I extracted the full PDF text directly (pypdf). Narrative: 'OPC supervises two pipeline projects extending from the Faiha oil field to the North Rumaila oil field in Al Basrah. The first pipeline is a 20-inch dry gas, and the second one is 10-inch LPG.' Table 1 row 7: 'Faiha oil field - Rumaila oil field | 20 (in) | 100 (km) | Dry gas'. (2) al-mirbad detail/163203: interview with the Faiha border oil field deputy manager Khalil Nahi (خليل ناهي) revealing 'the construction of two pipelines to transport dry gas and LPG, currently under construction' (إنشاء أنبوبين لنقل الغاز الجاف والغاز المسال قيد الإنجاز حاليا). These are independent origins (a compiled economist paper vs a field-management interview), not one wire story. CLASSIFICATION = correct: it is a gas (dry gas) line, Fuel=Gas correct; a field-to-NGL/grid dry-gas trunk, so PipelineType=transmission is defensible. FuelSource='Faiha oil field' confirmed (associated/dry gas off the Faiha field). Owner='Iraq Ministry of Oil' is reasonable — OPC (Oil Pipelines Company) and SCOP, the state entities building it, are Ministry of Oil bodies. DUPLICATE = none: the paired 10-inch line in the same sources is a separate LPG pipeline (different commodity), not a double-count of this 20-inch dry-gas row; and it is distinct from roster entries P6007 (West Qurna-Rumaila, dia 40) and P4041 (North Rumela-Al-Najaf). Diameter=20 in confirmed by the PDF (table + narrative). NOTE the North Rumaila endpoint is supported only by the PDF (al-mirbad names Faiha and the dry-gas/LPG pair but not Rumaila).

validity.researcher_notes: Capacity is recorded as 97.00 MMcf/d, cited to al-mirbad detail/163203 + a YouTube video. The value is NOT supported by its cited sources. Direct reading of al-mirbad: Khalil Nahi says the dry-gas line's production, per specialists, of 'around 100 MMSCFD (بحدود 100 مقمق) would be sufficient to produce around 700 MW' — i.e. ~100, not 97. The Al-Jibawi PDF narrative states the two projects 'will contribute to raising the dry gas pumping rate to 90 MMSCFD and the LPG pumping rate to 1100 tons per day' — i.e. 90. The prior verifier 'OK' on '97' for al-mirbad was a FALSE POSITIVE: the only '97' on the page is the site header radio frequency 'المثنى: 97.7'; the article body contains no 97. YouTube '97' is likewise an incidental substring, not a stated pipeline capacity. So two independent sources give ~90 and ~100 MMSCFD respectively and disagree with each other and with the sheet's 97; I did not stage a replacement number because the sources conflict, but 97 as recorded is unsupported.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=construction still correct. Al-Jibawi PDF (June 2025) lists it among projects OPC 'supervises' with future 'will contribute' framing = actively under construction; al-mirbad quotes the Faiha field deputy manager that the two pipelines are 'قيد الإنجاز حاليا' (currently under construction). Most recent reliably-dated independent evidence is the June-2025 PDF (al-mirbad publish date is not exposed in the page HTML — JS-rendered — but it predates the sheet's 2025-07-21 update). Searched Arabic and English for newer/operating evidence: a 2026-04-07 attaqa.net piece reports ongoing Basra dry-gas gathering work (a '20-inch accelerated gas' line, 55 MMscf/d, feeding the North Rumaila liquids-separation plant) but does not name the Faiha-North Rumaila line or declare it operating, so I did not treat it as a status change. Elapsed time from last evidence (mid-2025) to now (2026-07) is ~1 year — below the 2-year dormancy threshold — so no staleness downgrade; keep construction.
